name: Vaultwarden
description: Bitwarden-compatible password manager — self-hosted vault for passwords, notes, and 2FA, used with the Bitwarden browser and mobile apps
author: Crow

install_consent_messages.en: Vaultwarden stores the passwords and secrets for your entire digital life. Before you install: (1) this bundle will hold every credential you import, so back up ~/.crow/vaultwarden/data on a recurring schedule — losing it means losing everything; (2) Crow generates the admin token, keeps only its Argon2id hash in the extension's settings, and saves the token in Settings → Passwords (encrypted, this machine only); (3) sign-ups are CLOSED from install: Crow asks for your email below, invites it through Vaultwarden's own admin panel and only that address can create an account — you create the account in the web UI. Nobody else can register. The Crow MCP tools intentionally do NOT expose vault contents — use the official Bitwarden browser extension or mobile app as your working client.
install_consent_messages.es: Vaultwarden guardará las contraseñas y secretos de toda tu vida digital. Antes de instalar: (1) este bundle contendrá todas tus credenciales, haz copias de seguridad periódicas de ~/.crow/vaultwarden/data — perderlo significa perderlo todo; (2) Crow genera el token de administrador, guarda solo su hash Argon2id en la configuración de la extensión y guarda el token en Ajustes → Contraseñas (cifrado, solo en esta máquina); (3) los registros están CERRADOS desde la instalación: Crow te pide tu email abajo, lo invita a través del panel de administración de Vaultwarden y solo esa dirección puede crear una cuenta — la creas tú en la interfaz web. Nadie más puede registrarse. Las herramientas MCP de Crow intencionalmente NO exponen el contenido del vault — usa la extensión oficial de Bitwarden o la app móvil como cliente.

env_vars.name: VAULTWARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN
env_vars.description: Token for the /admin page. Crow generates it at install, keeps only an Argon2id hash in this extension's settings, saves the token itself in Settings → Passwords (encrypted, this machine only) and shows it to you once after install.

env_vars.name: VAULTWARDEN_DOMAIN
env_vars.description: Public URL Vaultwarden advertises to clients. Saving passwords to the vault from Crow needs this to be a secure https URL, e.g. https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port> from `sudo tailscale serve --bg --https=<port> http://127.0.0.1:8097` (see the Vaultwarden skill); also set it to https://... when put behind Caddy

env_vars.name: VAULTWARDEN_SIGNUPS_ALLOWED
env_vars.description: Whether new users can sign up in the web UI. Leave false: Crow invites your email and only invited people can create an account.

env_vars.name: VAULTWARDEN_OWNER_EMAIL
env_vars.description: The email you will create your Vaultwarden account with. Crow invites it at install; nobody else can sign up.

pattern_hint.es: una dirección de email como tu@example.com

firstAdmin.note: Crow invites your email at install, so only that address can create an account.

notes: Invite-only from install: sign-ups are closed, Crow invites the email you give it through Vaultwarden's admin panel, and you create the account in the web UI. See the skill for the recommended setup order (invite → create account → back up data dir). The MCP tools are deliberately minimal: status, user_count, backup_info. They do NOT read vault contents — use the Bitwarden browser extension or mobile app for day-to-day password access.
